page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs using the AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-threaded performance. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by the stress-ng single-core CPU performance in the bottom 10% and single-threaded gzip compression in the bottom 25%. However, the instance demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities, with its PassMark CPU score, extended instructions test, and encryption test all ranking in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression also performs strongly in the top 25% at 251.92 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 52.74 million operations per second, consistently rank in the average tier.

Given its high core density and dedicated CPU allocation, the ecs.c6a.16xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for parallelized, compute-heavy workloads that do not require local storage or high per-core memory ratios. The lack of bundled local storage means storage costs are decoupled, allowing users to scale block storage independently. This instance is well-suited for highly parallelized workloads such as multi-threaded data decompression, cryptography, batch processing, and web serving.
